Fix the following bug in this repository (oneDAL). Build and run the C++ tests with `bazel` (on PATH); this machine has no GPU and no oneAPI compiler, so use the `*_host` targets. Do not weaken or delete existing tests.

# k-means++ init: the best local trial's candidate is not scored with its own point

The k-means++ initialization (`kmeans_init`, CPU, dense and CSR input) draws several candidate centers per step ("local trials") and keeps the one that lowers the potential the most. After each step, the minimum squared distances of every row are updated for every trial. For the trial that won the previous step, the update goes wrong: its distance slot is scored with the candidate of trial 0 instead of its own candidate. Whenever the previous winner is not trial 0, one candidate is never scored properly, and it ties with trial 0 up to last-bit rounding. The pick then depends on rounding, which differs between the dense and CSR distance formulas and between instruction sets, so dense and CSR results can disagree.

The bug is in the block update helpers of `cpp/daal/src/algorithms/kmeans/kmeans_plusplus_init_impl.i` (the dense and CSR `updateMinDistInBlock`-style helpers). The expected behaviour: every trial's distance slot is updated with that trial's own candidate, the previous best trial included, and every slot starts from the previous best trial's distances.

The test `cpp/oneapi/dal/algo/kmeans_init/test/internal.cpp` (target `test_internal_host`) checks the kernel's helper directly. Do not change the test to make it pass. Please report the root cause in your final answer.
